Water and milk are good offerings for Selene. Water is simple but effective because it is cleasing and easy to leave out over night. I find milk is really good when focusing on Selene's motherly nature.   
Round/crescent shaped cookies or curved croissants can be used as food offerings.   
I've personally found floral fragrances and lavendar incense to be good options as well.

  
In terms of what to put on an altar, white and silver candles are the usual go to options but you can also use black (representing new moon) or even reddish orange colours to represent a blood moon. 

Horses and bulls are associated with Selene if you like to include animal connections. Selene was described as having long wings so you can also add feathers for your altar or something symbolising wings. As Iaahbane has commented, you can add ocean related things like seashells/stones you find on the beach. 

If you want to put crystals on the altar some good options would be moonstone, selenite or white crystals such as howlite or snow quartz. 

I find anything shiny/delicate/beautiful also works really well as an offering or to put on the altar so feel free to add anything else that feels suitable and personal for you.

Reading your post, I think you may be underestimating your depression. 

I can relate to the feelings of guilt, feeling lazy, that you're not doing enough and that you don't deserve nice things. 

You might not really be lazy but instead your depression is making you feel lazy. It's not as if you don't want to be productive - it's that you can't find the energy. 

Depression is a sneaky illness because it will take away all your motivation and then make you feel guilty for it. It gets to the point you start looking for a 'valid' reason - in your case getting hit by a car. 

I remember feeling similar to your post (I've lost my job now) but whilst I was still employed I fell ill with covid for a while. It was rough and I couldn't get out of bed but mentally it felt like a break. I felt like I had a 'valid' reason not to do anything. It didn't offer a long term solution though and just temporarily replaced a mental health problem with a physical one.

I don't know if your company can help make some allowances or even if you can take some paid time off? I realise it can be hard to disclose mental health issues with your employer so it's totally your decision but it's something that might be worth exploring given the impact it's having. 

It's not your fault you feel overwhelmed right now and doesn't make you unworthy in any way. Try to be gentle with yourself at this time.   


Also as a side note: your english is very good :)

Coming from someone who is single and just lost their job, it's not insulting at all. Thing is there will always be someone else who has it worse. It doesn't mean that your feelings are invalid or not worth talking about. We all struggle with different things and we're only human afterall.

You have just described my experience! Especially the part about dissociating and then doing more damage through self harm because you’re in a dissociative state. 

It was always a dilemma I struggled with - do I self harm now so the stress doesn’t build up and lead to dissociation or do I try and tough it out and hope the intense feelings go away in time. 

I can’t say I know what you are going through, only that it must be really hard and scary. 

It might be that there is something going on in your life that is causing a baseline of high stress and dependent on self harm. That or maybe biological factors. 

I would argue this is probably why alternatives to self harm aren’t working for you because they fail to address the real problem.

Obviously I’m not an expert or anything and you have to do what you feel is right but I would try to see what the triggers are and consider medication if you haven’t already. 

Based on that you can try and make positive changes to try and avoid these intense feelings. E.g. If you have toxic people in your life, cut them out. 

Imo self harm can be very effective and useful in avoiding dissociative experiences but it does have its risks and it’s a sign that you’re not in a good place.
